mappings.note: 'mukhya roop se' asks what the poem chiefly says - LO-106, forming a sense of the composition's subject. Rejected LO-107, which is for a specific point inside it.

Asks whom the quoted lines address - locating the addressee in the poem, LO-107. NB the item is broken twice over: options (A) and (B) are identical ('toofan se'), there is no correct-option marker, and the printed answer ('manushyon se') is not among the four options at all.
The poet's year of birth, from the kavi-parichay - a specific point in the printed material, LO-107.
Paryayavachi of 'timir' - a pure word-meaning item, LO-110. Rejected LO-115, which covers figures and metre rather than synonym sets.
Where power is said to reside (vigyan) is stated in the poem. LO-107.
'dhara ka arth' is a word-meaning item. LO-110.
The poet's year of death, from the kavi-parichay. LO-107.
Match-the-following glossing amavas, purnima, vidyut-diye and yug - unfamiliar words and their meanings, LO-110. Rejected LO-107: the work is lexical.
Matches the poem's lines to their bhav - reading each line's figurative sense, LO-115. Rejected LO-110, since whole lines rather than words are glossed.

Fill-in choosing the poet's own word from three synonyms (naiya / naav / nauka) - a question about the line's diction and rhythm, so LO-115 rather than LO-110, which is about meaning. NB the chapter contradicts itself: this key says 'naiya' while the padyansh item prints the same line as 'bahate chalo naav tum vah nirantar'.
Fill-in choosing between tat / teer / kinara - the poet's diction and the line's rhyme, LO-115.
Fill-in choosing between dhara / dharti / bhoomi - diction and metre, LO-115.
Fill-in choosing between praat / subah / savera - diction and rhyme, LO-115.
Fill-in choosing between andhkar / timir / andhere - the poet's word choice, LO-115.
Fill-in choosing between pratham / avval / pehli - diction, LO-115. These six fill-ins form one set on recalling the poem's exact wording.

Asks which images the poem uses for darkness (amavas, nisha, timir ki sarita, timir ki shila, pavan, toofan) - an inventory of its figures, LO-115. Rejected LO-107, which would be satisfied by a single stated detail.
What hope the poem holds out and why - the whole composition's message, LO-106 rather than LO-107.
Answers from the shabdarth note on 'purnima' rather than from the poem's lines - a word-meaning item, LO-110.
The poet's suggestions for dispelling darkness are stated in the lines. LO-107.
'apne vichar likhiye' on which values the poem teaches and why they are needed today - the pupil's own written comment, LO-117. Rejected LO-106, since the second half is argued from outside the poem.
What is to be lit and what put out is stated in the poem. LO-107.

A class-sharing activity - LO-104 covers carrying forward conversation about what has been read. NB the item is an orphan fragment: the list-making half it refers to is not in the bank, and the 'answer' is only a note that pupils do it themselves.
The poet's name is printed with the poem - locating it, LO-107.
What the poet asks to be lit ('sneh ke diye') is his own phrase. LO-107; rejected LO-115, as the pupil only has to find it.
How the world will become beautiful is the poem's whole argument - LO-106.
'kavita aapko kaise prerit karti hai' asks for the pupil's own written response, LO-117 rather than LO-107.
Which story continues (the lamp and the storm) is stated in the poem. LO-107.
Crossing the river of darkness works only through the poem's boat-of-lamps figure - LO-115's appreciation of poetic imagery over LO-107.
Padyansh with five sub-questions: most are comprehension (LO-107), but Q3 asks what amavas SYMBOLISES (LO-115). Both cited so neither half is left unmapped.
Padyansh whose sub-questions mix comprehension (LO-107) with what 'timir' symbolises (LO-115).
Padyansh with comprehension sub-questions (LO-107) plus a paryayavachi question on 'pavan' and a gloss of 'anginat' (LO-110). NB sub-answer 4 carries a stray 'prashn' label bled into the key.
Padyansh whose Q1 names the alankar ('svarn-si' = upma) and Q4 restores the exact line (LO-115, the fine points of poetic language), while Q2 asks paryayavachi of 'nisha' (LO-110).
